newsitem.title: USA: U.S. corporate bond spreads widen marginally.
newsitem.headline: U.S. corporate bond spreads widen marginally.

text.p: U.S. investment grade corporate bond spreads widened marginally on Friday as Treasuries rallied on allayed fears of inflation and a Federal Reserve interest rate hike, traders said.
Corporate bond trade was described as extremely light in the aftermath of more than $5 billion of new investment grade supply on the week, however.
Turning to high-yields, prices were quoted higher by 1/2 point on average with respect to an extension of weakness in the paper and supermarket sectors.

Claridge Hotels and Casino's 11-3/4 percent notes put in the star performance for the day, meanwhile, rising nearly 10 points after the company said it was in acquisition talks with the Hilton Hotels Corp.
The notes were quoted 77-5/8 bid, 78-3/8 offer near the close, traders said, up 9-3/8 on the bid. More than $3 million Claridge notes had traded.

The issue had been mired in the 60s since the company said in November it was unlikely it would be able to make its February 1 interest payment. While Claridge said that payment will not be made, prices rose as Hilton said its proposal would include a buyback of the notes it does not own at a 10 percent premium, traders and analysts said.

Elsewhere, Stone Container debt dropped one point on Friday on the heels of a two point drop on Thursday, traders said. Bondholders were increasingly wary of the credit, traders said, based on deteriorating fundamentals in the industry and expected weak earnings.
In addition, Stone on Monday filed a shelf registration with the Securities and Exchange Commission to sell up to $1.0 billion in debt securities.
Crown Paper 11s were down two to three points on the week to 92-1/4 bid, 92-3/4 offer.

Back in investment grades, traders reported lackluster activity as the Street continued to talk of the mass of new issues priced this week. Big issues, all handily placed, included $2.0 billion "four B" Tenet Healthcare's, $1.0 billion GMAC five-years and $500 million GTE 30-years.
One retail trader reported light retail selling. Despite the fact corporates couldn't keep pace with rallying Treasuries, traders insisted market tone was intact.

Treasuries were lifted early following lenient inflation signs in the report of fourth quarter gross domestic product, analysts there said. The market shrugged off the stronger than expected Q4 GDP rise of 4.7 percent, leaving the Street doubting a rate hike at next week's meeting of the Federal Open Market Committee.
New issuance tapered off on Friday with only a few deals priced. Investment grade issues priced on Friday included:
--$150 million 30-year capital securities from BanPonce Trust I, priced to yield 145 basis points over the Treasury curve via Credit Suisse First Boston.
--$100 million seven-year 7-1/8 percent senior notes, priced to yield 80 basis points over Treasuries via lead manager Merrill Lynch & Co Inc.

--$425 million in 10-1/8 percent seven-year senior notes and 10.50 percent 10-year senior notes from Mexico's TV Azteca, priced in the 144A market via Bear, Stearns & Co. The seven-year notes were priced to yield 375 basis points over Treasuries and the 10-year notes were priced at 400 over.

On the horizon, Tele-Communications Inc spin-off TCI Satellite Entertainment will issue over the next few weeks $350 million in debt to finance the growth of its medium- and high-powered digital broadcast (DBS) services.
